sentences.text:
Applicant :- Patali
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Faiz Ahmad
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Faiz Ahmad, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur,
learned AGA for the State-respondent.
2.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
131 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 302 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Mohabbatpur Paisa,
District Kaushambi, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and according to the FIR marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the sister of the informant and after marriage applicant used to torture her and on 10.11.2023 he made assault upon her due to which she died.
4.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that however, applicant is husband of the deceased but on the basis of false allegations, he has been made accused in the present matter.

Patali vs State Of U.P. on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26350611/
1 5.

He further submitted that actually deceased accidentally fell down and sustained injuries and died and after her death, on the basis of false allegations, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.
6. He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 13.11.2023.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and post mortem report also suggests that deceased sustained two crushed injuries and due to crushed injuries, she died and applicant did not explain how she sustained crushed injuries in her matrimonial home.
8.
He next submitted that apart from the present case, applicant is also having criminal history of two other cases but also he did not explain his previous criminal history.
He further submitted that therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, applicant should not be released on bail.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. However, it reflects that applicant is in jail in the present matter since November, 2023 i.e. for last more than a year but he is husband of the deceased and his wife was found dead in her matrimonial home and as per allegation, applicant committed her murder and post mortem report of the deceased which has been produced by learned AGA, during the course of argument, suggests that deceased died due to ante mortem injuries and she sustained two crushed injuries.
Applicant failed to explain the ante mortem injuries sustained by his wife.
Further, it appears apart from the present case applicant is also having criminal history of two other cases.
Therefore, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
11. Accordingly, the instant bail application stands rejected, at this stage.

12. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 9.4.2025
